One man survived both atomic bombs.
In August 1945, an engineer named Tsutomu Yamaguchi was in Hiroshima on a business trip.
On his last day there, he was walking to the shipyard when he heard a plane.
Then, a flash brighter than the sun.
He was about three kilometres away. The blast threw him to the ground and burned his skin.
He spent the night in a shelter. The next day, he took a train home.
On August the ninth, covered in bandages, he went back to work.
He told his boss about the giant flash. His boss said one bomb could never destroy a whole city.
At that moment, the second bomb exploded over Nagasaki.
Again, he was about three kilometres away. And again, he survived.
He lived to be ninety three, and spent his last years speaking out against nuclear weapons.
